w: Designed by Stanislaw Szpakowski and built 1901-1903 on land donated by Mojzesz Pfefer, this synagogue was desecrated by the Nazis in WWII and used as a prison and storage depot for looted Jewish property. Empty from 1945 to 1951, it was seized by the communist state for the State Archives, which still occupy it.
s: Desecrated synagogue turned Nazi prison, now the state archive
_facts: Designed by Stanislaw Szpakowski, built 1901-1903
Desecrated by Nazis in WWII; used as prison and storage for stolen Jewish property
Stood empty 1945-1951, then taken over by the State Archives (still there in 2019)
Adjoining mikvah and rabbi's house demolished in the 1970s

w: Founded in the 12th century by Krakow's Bishop Gedeon, destroyed by Tatars in 1260, rebuilt from 1719 in early Baroque under Bishop Kazimierz Lubienski. Inside, a Baroque-rococo high altar by Fontana. Cathedral of the Diocese of Kielce since 1805, and shrine to an icon crowned in 1636, re-crowned 1872 after theft.
s: Baroque cathedral on Castle Hill, rebuilt after Tatar razing
_facts: Founded 12th century by Bishop Gedeon of Krakow; destroyed by Tatars in 1260
Rebuilt from 1719 in early Baroque under Bishop Kazimierz Lubienski
High altar by Fontana; became cathedral of the new Diocese of Kielce in 1805
Shrine of Our Lady of Graces, icon crowned 1636 and re-crowned 1872

n: Palace of the Krakow Bishops in Kielce
w: Built in the 17th century as a summer residence for the Bishops of Krakow, this palace mixes Polish and Italian architectural traditions, reflecting its founder's political ambitions. It stands on Kielce's Castle Hill beside the cathedral and now houses a National Museum branch hung with Polish paintings.
s: Baroque bishops' summer palace turned Polish painting gallery
_facts: Built 17th century as a summer residence for the Bishops of Krakow
Mixes Polish and Italian architectural traditions
Now houses a branch of the National Museum with a gallery of Polish paintings

w: Known locally as the Pakosz Cemetery, this 3.12-hectare Jewish burial ground sits at the junction of Pakosz Dolny and Kusocinskiego streets. About 330 tombstones survive, roughly 150 gathered into a single lapidary monument rather than left standing in original plots. Closed without a special permit.
s: Pakosz district burial ground, 330 tombstones behind locked gates
_facts: Also known as the Pakosz Cemetery
3.12 hectares, at Pakosz Dolny and Kusocinskiego streets
About 330 tombstones preserved, ~150 arranged into a lapidary monument
Closed to visitors without special permit

w: Unveiled on the fifth anniversary of September 11, 2001, this was the first monument in Europe to commemorate the attacks' victims. Sculptor Adam Myjak built it from two seven-metre pillars leaning toward each other, criss-crossed by two planes and bearing plates naming the stricken cities.
s: Europe's first 9/11 memorial, two leaning seven-metre pillars
_facts: First monument in Europe commemorating 9/11 victims
Designed by Adam Myjak, unveiled September 11, 2006
Two seven-metre pillars, criss-crossed by two planes, naming the attacked cities
George W. Bush's letter to Kielce was read at the unveiling

w: Kielce's main commercial spine, built in the mid-19th century as ulica Konstantego, then Postal Street, before taking its current name in 1919. Running about 1270 metres from the railway station at Independence Square to Moniuszko Square, it is lined with department stores, shops, historic buildings and monuments.
s: Kielce's historic high street, renamed three times since 1919
_facts: Built mid-19th century; originally ulica Konstantego, then Postal Street
Took its present name, honouring Henryk Sienkiewicz, in 1919
About 1270 metres, from the railway station/Independence Square to Moniuszko Square

w: Considered the oldest sacred site in Kielce, predating the city's own founding charter, this church stands on ground tradition holds as the martyrdom site of Saint Adalbert. The complex includes a manor house and clergy house, and the interior holds works by painter Jan Styka.
s: Kielce's oldest church, said to mark a saint's martyrdom
_facts: Oldest sacral monument in Kielce, predating the city's founding rights
Tradition holds it as the site of Saint Adalbert's martyrdom
Complex includes a manor house and clergy house; interior works by Jan Styka
Protected on Poland's register of historic monuments
